questions.question: Which AWS service provides a fully managed environment to build, train, and deploy machine learning models at scale?
questions.explanation: Amazon SageMaker is AWS's end-to-end managed ML platform, covering data labeling, training, tuning, hosting and monitoring of custom models. Amazon Rekognition is a pre-trained vision API you call rather than train. Amazon Bedrock exposes pre-trained foundation models via an API and supports light fine-tuning, but it is not AWS's general platform for building, training and deploying arbitrary custom ML models from scratch. Amazon Comprehend is a pre-trained NLP API and exposes no training/deployment surface for custom models.

questions.question: Which Amazon service is purpose-built for generative AI applications using foundation models from multiple providers via a single API?
questions.explanation: Amazon Bedrock exposes foundation models from multiple providers — Anthropic Claude, Meta Llama, Mistral, Cohere, AI21 and Amazon Titan — through one serverless API. Amazon Lex builds conversational chatbots on a single NLU model. Amazon Forecast produces time-series forecasts, and Amazon Polly converts text to speech; none of them offers multi-provider foundation-model access.

questions.question: A company wants to extract entities, key phrases and sentiment from customer support tickets. Which AWS service is the best fit?
questions.explanation: Amazon Comprehend is the managed NLP service that detects entities, key phrases, language, sentiment and PII in text. Amazon Translate performs machine translation between languages. Amazon Transcribe converts speech audio to text. Amazon Textract extracts text, forms and tables from scanned documents — a document-understanding OCR pipeline, not a sentiment or entity analyser — so it is a common near-miss for teams that want to "pull structure out of text" but need semantic analysis rather than layout extraction.

questions.question: A team is integrating a large language model into a customer-support assistant. They notice that small changes in how they word the request — adding examples, specifying tone, asking the model to think step by step — dramatically change the output quality without changing model weights. Which discipline are they applying?
questions.explanation: Prompt engineering is the practice of designing a model's text input — instructions, examples, formatting and step-by-step cues — so a foundation model produces accurate, on-task output without altering its weights. Model distillation trains a smaller model to mimic a larger one, changing the model itself. RLHF fine-tuning updates model weights using human preference signals during a training stage, not at request time. Hyperparameter tuning searches training settings such as learning rate; all three change the model or its training rather than the prompt.

questions.question: A product team has a public LLM that has no knowledge of internal product manuals updated last week. They want answers grounded in those manuals without retraining the model. Their solution: index the manuals, retrieve top passages by similarity at request time, and inject them into the prompt as context. Which technique is this?
questions.explanation: Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) indexes documents, retrieves the most relevant passages by similarity at request time and injects them into the prompt as context, grounding answers in private or fresh data without retraining. RLHF tunes model weights from human preference data during training, not per request. Knowledge distillation compresses a large model into a smaller one. Few-shot prompting adds a few example pairs to the prompt but has no retrieval step over an external corpus.

questions.question: A team wants to store embeddings to power a semantic search feature on top of Amazon Bedrock. Which AWS service provides a managed vector database capability?
questions.explanation: Amazon OpenSearch Service includes a k-NN and vector engine for storing and querying embeddings, making it a managed vector store for semantic search. Amazon Neptune (property-graph / RDF) answers relationship queries, not similarity queries over embeddings. AWS Glue Data Catalog is a metadata catalog for datasets in S3 — it stores table definitions and schema, not vectors. Amazon DynamoDB is a key-value and document NoSQL database with no native similarity search. (Aurora PostgreSQL with pgvector and Amazon MemoryDB also support vectors, but they are not among the options.)

questions.question: Which AWS Generative AI service is an enterprise assistant that can be grounded on a company's own data and integrated into business workflows?
questions.explanation: Amazon Q Business is a generative-AI assistant for work that connects to enterprise data sources such as S3, Confluence and Salesforce, answering questions and taking actions while respecting each user's access permissions. Amazon Lex builds custom conversational chatbots — you design the intents and flow yourself, and it ships with no enterprise data connectors. Amazon Personalize generates product recommendations, and Amazon Polly is text-to-speech — neither is an enterprise assistant.

questions.question: A team is choosing the right ML paradigm for a fraud-detection problem. They have a large historical dataset where each past transaction is labelled fraud or legitimate by investigators. They want a model that learns to predict the label on new transactions. Which paradigm fits?
questions.explanation: Supervised learning trains on labelled input-output pairs and then predicts the label for new, unseen inputs — exactly the fraud-versus-legitimate setup described. Rule-based scoring hand-codes if/then thresholds; it can score transactions but nothing is *learned* from data, which the scenario explicitly requires. Reinforcement learning learns from reward signals while interacting with an environment. Unsupervised learning works on unlabelled data to find clusters or anomalies — it ignores the labels the investigators already assigned.

questions.question: A model performs extremely well on the training set but poorly on unseen data. What is this called?
questions.explanation: Overfitting means the model has memorized the training data, including its noise, so it generalizes poorly to new data. Underfitting is the opposite — a model too simple to capture the pattern, so it does poorly even on training data. Data drift is a change in the input distribution after deployment, not a training/test gap on a static split. Bias is a systematic error from flawed assumptions or unrepresentative data; none of these describes strong training performance paired with weak performance on unseen data.

questions.question: A regulated lender deploys a credit-scoring model and must demonstrate to auditors which features drove each decision and whether the model exhibits bias across demographic groups. AWS markets a service that surfaces feature attributions and bias metrics across the model lifecycle. Which service is it?
questions.explanation: Amazon SageMaker Clarify detects bias in data and models and uses SHAP values to produce per-feature attributions, letting auditors see what drove each prediction. Amazon SageMaker Model Cards document a model's intended use, training data and known limitations as static governance artifacts — they record what a team claims about a model, but they do not actively compute bias metrics or feature attributions. Amazon Comprehend is an NLP service for entities and sentiment, and Amazon Rekognition analyses images and video — neither measures bias or explainability.

questions.question: A media app needs to convert article text into natural-sounding speech in multiple languages and voices. The team wants a managed AWS service that handles neural text-to-speech without operating their own infrastructure. Which service does this?
questions.explanation: Amazon Polly is the managed neural text-to-speech service, converting text into lifelike speech across many languages and voices. Amazon Transcribe does the reverse — speech to text. Amazon Translate performs text translation between languages. Amazon Lex builds conversational chatbots; it uses speech recognition and language understanding but is not a text-to-speech engine.

questions.question: A retailer wants per-user product recommendations as a managed service. They don't want to design embeddings or train models themselves — they will hand AWS their interaction events (views, purchases) and the catalogue, and consume a real-time API. Which AWS service does this?
questions.explanation: Amazon Personalize is a managed recommendation service: you supply interaction events and a catalogue and consume a real-time recommendations API without building models yourself. Amazon Forecast produces time-series forecasts (sales, demand, capacity) — it predicts numeric values over time, not per-user picks. Amazon Kendra is an enterprise search service that ranks documents for a query, not products for a user. Amazon Lookout for Metrics detects anomalies in business metrics — an alerting layer, not a recommender.

questions.question: A company evaluating generative-AI patterns wants a precise definition of a foundation model so non-technical stakeholders can contrast it with other ML approaches such as narrow classifiers, rules engines and federated training. Which option BEST describes a foundation model?
options: A handcrafted rules engine assembled by domain experts, with no statistical training and no ability to generalize beyond its rules
A narrow single-task model trained from scratch on a small labelled dataset for one specific business objective
A federated learning algorithm that trains a model only on edge devices to preserve raw data privacy by design
A large model pretrained on broad unlabelled data, then adapted to many tasks via prompting, RAG or fine-tuning
questions.explanation: A foundation model is a large model pretrained on broad, mostly unlabelled data that can be adapted to many downstream tasks — text, code, images — via prompting, RAG or fine-tuning. A narrow single-task model is the opposite: trained on a small labelled set for one job. A handcrafted rules engine has no statistical training component. Federated learning is a distributed training approach for private data, not a definition of a foundation model.

questions.question: A bank already has a public LLM answering well over their indexed compliance manuals via retrieval-augmented generation. Now they want the model itself to adopt their specific tone, terminology, and structured response format consistently across all answers — beyond what context injection achieves. When should fine-tuning be preferred over RAG?
options: When the underlying knowledge changes daily, so the model can absorb each update without an index rebuild
When the model itself must consistently adopt a specific tone, vocabulary and response format across every answer it produces
When the assistant must store a small list of frequently-changing policy values, since fine-tuning reliably memorizes those facts verbatim
When inference cost is the priority, since a fine-tuned model never benefits from caching retrieved passages
questions.explanation: Fine-tuning is preferred when the model itself must consistently adopt a stable behaviour — tone, domain vocabulary or response format — across all answers, beyond what prompt context alone can guarantee. Fine-tuning does not reliably memorize discrete facts; it teaches patterns and style, and changing facts still belong in a retrieval index. For knowledge that changes frequently, RAG is better because you update only the document store. And fine-tuning is not automatically cheaper at inference: it carries training cost up front and must be repeated whenever the desired behaviour changes.

questions.question: Which AWS Bedrock feature lets you create a managed knowledge base and have a model answer questions grounded on your private documents?
questions.explanation: Knowledge Bases for Amazon Bedrock provides a managed RAG pipeline — it ingests documents, chunks and embeds them, stores the vectors, and lets a model answer questions grounded on that private data. Bedrock Guardrails enforces content-safety policies (denied topics, PII, contextual grounding checks) rather than sourcing answers. Bedrock Model Evaluation compares model quality on benchmarks or human review, and Bedrock Provisioned Throughput reserves dedicated inference capacity for predictable latency — neither builds a knowledge base.

questions.question: Which Bedrock feature helps block harmful content, profanity, prompt injection, and topics you do not want a model to discuss?
questions.explanation: Bedrock Guardrails lets you define content filters, denied topics, word filters, sensitive-information (PII) filters and contextual-grounding checks to block harmful or unwanted model output. Bedrock Agents orchestrate multi-step tasks and tool calls — they act, but they do not filter output. Bedrock Knowledge Bases add RAG grounding, and Bedrock Studio is a collaborative app-building workspace — neither is the content-safety control layer.

questions.question: A team trained a binary classifier on a highly imbalanced fraud dataset (1% positive). Accuracy looks great at 99% but the model is useless because it predicts 'not fraud' constantly. Which metric is MOST appropriate to evaluate this binary classifier on imbalanced data?
options: F1 score on the positive (fraud) class, balancing precision and recall on the rare label
Mean squared error between predicted and actual class labels across the full record set
Overall accuracy computed across every record in the test set, regardless of class balance
The value of the training cross-entropy loss observed at the end of training, with no validation split
questions.explanation: The F1 score on the positive class combines precision and recall on the fraud class, so it stays meaningful even when 99% of records belong to the negative class — and the area under the precision-recall curve behaves similarly. Overall accuracy is misleading here, since always predicting 'not fraud' already scores 99%. Mean squared error is a regression metric and does not apply to discrete classification. The training cross-entropy loss is an optimization signal, not a measure of how well the classifier identifies the rare class.

questions.question: Under the AWS Shared Responsibility Model for AI services such as Amazon Bedrock, which task remains the customer's responsibility?
options: Patching the operating systems and GPU drivers of the hosts that run the foundation models
Designing the prompts, curating any fine-tuning data, and evaluating whether the model's outputs meet the use case
Maintaining the foundation model's weights and the underlying inference infrastructure
Continuously retraining the hosted foundation models on new public corpora and benchmarks
questions.explanation: Under the shared responsibility model, AWS operates the infrastructure — host operating systems, hardware, and the hosted foundation models themselves, including any retraining of those base models. The customer remains responsible for how the service is used: the prompts they send, any fine-tuning data they supply, and evaluating model outputs for their application. Patching the GPU host operating systems, maintaining the foundation model weights and inference infrastructure, and continuously retraining the hosted models are all AWS responsibilities.

questions.question: A team building a customer-facing generative-AI assistant wants to align its design with the AWS Responsible AI framework before launch, and is comparing several proposed working principles to decide which one to adopt. Which option captures a key principle of Responsible AI on AWS?
options: Choosing the largest foundation model available for customer-facing tasks to guarantee fairness by scale alone
Replacing human reviewers with fixed acceptance thresholds so behaviour stays reproducible end to end
Building AI that is fair, explainable, privacy-preserving, secure, robust and subject to human oversight
Treating fairness review as a one-time pre-launch audit instead of a continuing post-deployment program
questions.explanation: AWS frames Responsible AI around dimensions such as fairness, explainability, privacy, security, robustness, governance and transparency, with human oversight throughout — and SageMaker Clarify, Bedrock Guardrails and model cards help operationalize them. Picking the largest model does not guarantee fairness; scale can even amplify bias on under-represented groups. Replacing human reviewers with thresholds eliminates the human-oversight control the framework requires. A one-time pre-launch fairness audit ignores that drift, data shifts and new edge cases can change bias profiles after deployment, so AWS calls for ongoing measurement rather than a single sign-off.

questions.question: A solutions architect needs to call a foundation model from a Lambda function with the lowest operational overhead. Which approach is best?
options: Call the Amazon Bedrock runtime InvokeModel API on-demand from Lambda to invoke a foundation model
Train a custom model in SageMaker and host it on a real-time SageMaker endpoint invoked from Lambda
Self-host the foundation model on EC2 GPU instances behind an Application Load Balancer fronted by Lambda
Reserve Bedrock Provisioned Throughput for the model and call that dedicated reserved capacity from Lambda
questions.explanation: Calling the Amazon Bedrock runtime API (InvokeModel or Converse) on-demand from Lambda gives true serverless model access with no provisioning, scaling or capacity planning — the lowest operational overhead. Bedrock Provisioned Throughput reserves dedicated capacity by model units for predictable latency on high-volume workloads; it adds capacity-planning, reservation and commitment overhead that on-demand avoids. A SageMaker real-time endpoint means training and hosting a model yourself. EC2 GPU instances behind a load balancer require provisioning, patching and scaling infrastructure, which is far more operational work.
